entries.sanskrit:
सप्त-विंशे ततः सम्यग् बहु-साधन-योगतः ।

पुं-प्रकृत्योर् विवेकेन मोक्ष-रीतिर् निरूप्यते ॥

विवेक-ज्ञानेन मोक्षम् उपपादयितुं शुद्धस्यैव पुरुषस्य प्रकृत्य्-अविवेकतः पूर्वोक्तं संसारम् अनुस्मारयति---प्रकृति-स्थोऽपीति त्रिभिः । देह-स्थोऽपि नाज्यते न लिप्यते। गुणैस् तत् कृतैः सुख-दुःखादिभिः । निर्गुणत्वाद् अकर्तृत्वं ततोऽविकारित्वं तस्मात् ॥१॥
word_for_word: then, completely, through the means of many practices
through discrimination between Puruṣa and Prakṛti
the method of liberation is described
to establish liberation through discriminative knowledge
he recalls the previously described saṃsāra arising from non-discrimination from Prakṛti
although dwelling in the body, he is neither delighted nor stained
by happiness, distress, and other things produced by the guṇas
because he is without guṇas, [there is] non-agency
entries.literal_english: in the twenty-seventh [chapter]; then, completely, through the means of many practices; through discrimination between Puruṣa and Prakṛti; the method of liberation is described; to establish liberation through discriminative knowledge; of the pure Puruṣa alone; he recalls the previously described saṃsāra arising from non-discrimination from Prakṛti; although dwelling in the body, he is neither delighted nor stained; by happiness, distress, and other things produced by the guṇas; because he is without guṇas, [there is] non-agency; therefore immutability, for that reason

sapta-viṃśe tataḥ samyag bahu-sādhana-yogataḥ |

puṃ-prakṛtyor vivekena mokṣa-rītir nirūpyate ||

viveka-jñānena mokṣam upapādayituṃ śuddhasyaiva puruṣasya prakṛty-avivekataḥ pūrvoktaṃ saṃsāram anusmārayati---prakṛti-stho’pīti tribhiḥ | deha-stho’pi nājyate na lipyate| guṇais tat kṛtaiḥ sukha-duḥkhādibhiḥ | nirguṇatvād akartṛtvaṃ tato’vikāritvaṃ tasmāt ||1||

entries.sanskrit: यतो विषय-ध्यानम् अर्थ-हेतुः, अतो मनो नियन्तव्यम् इत्य् आह---अत एवेति । असताम् इन्द्रियाणां पथि विषय-मार्गे । तीव्रेन दृढेन । विरक्त्या च तीव्रया ॥५॥
word_for_word: because meditation on sense objects is the cause of attainment
therefore the mind must be restrained—he says
on the path of uncontrolled senses
on the road of sense objects
entries.literal_english: because meditation on sense objects is the cause of attainment; therefore the mind must be restrained—he says; on the path of uncontrolled senses; on the road of sense objects; with intense, firm [control]; and with intense detachment

entries.sanskrit: भक्ति-विरक्त्योस् तीव्रत्वे कारणानि वर्णयन् ज्ञानेन मोक्ष-प्रकारम् आह षड्भिः । यमादिभिर् योग-मार्गैश् चित्तम् अभ्यसन् पुनः पुनर् एकाग्री-कुर्वन्न् आत्मानम् उपलभ्य सर्वानुस्यूतम् अद्वयं परमात्मानं प्रतिपद्यत इति षष्ठेनान्वयः । सत्येन निष्कपटेन । भावेन प्रेम्णा ॥६॥
word_for_word: describing the causes of the intensity of devotion and detachment
he explains the means of liberation through knowledge in six [verses]
practicing the mind through the paths of yoga beginning with yama
making it one-pointed again and again
he attains the nondual Supreme Self pervading all
entries.literal_english: describing the causes of the intensity of devotion and detachment; he explains the means of liberation through knowledge in six [verses]; practicing the mind through the paths of yoga beginning with yama; making it one-pointed again and again; having realized the Self; he attains the nondual Supreme Self pervading all; with truth, without deceit; with feeling, with love

entries.transliteration: bhakti-viraktyos tīvratve kāraṇāni varṇayan jñānena mokṣa-prakāram āha ṣaḍbhiḥ | yamādibhir yoga-mārgaiś cittam abhyasan punaḥ punar ekāgrī-kurvann ātmānam upalabhya sarvānusyūtam advayaṃ paramātmānaṃ pratipadyata iti ṣaṣṭhenānvayaḥ | satyena niṣkapaṭena | bhāvena premṇā ||6||

entries.sanskrit: निवृत्तानि बुद्ध्य्-अवस्थानानि जाग्रद्-आदीनि यस्य सः । अत एव दूरी-भूतम् अन्य-दर्शनं यस्य । आत्मनाहङ्कारावच्छिन्नेनात्मानं शुद्धम् उपलभ्य । एकस्यैवावच्छेदानवच्छेदाभ्यां करण-कर्मत्वे दृष्टान्तम् आह---चक्षुषा चक्षुर्-अवच्छिन्नेनार्केण गगन-स्थम् अर्कम् इव । एवम् आत्म-दृक् शुद्धम् आत्मानं पश्यन् ॥१०॥
word_for_word: one whose states of intellect, waking and the rest, have ceased
therefore, one for whom perception of anything else has gone far away
having realized the pure Self by the Self limited by ego
for the one [Self], instrumenthood and objecthood through limitation and non-limitation
with the sun limited by the eye, as the eye
like the sun situated in the sky
thus seeing the pure Self, the seer of the Self
entries.literal_english: one whose states of intellect, waking and the rest, have ceased; therefore, one for whom perception of anything else has gone far away; having realized the pure Self by the Self limited by ego; for the one [Self], instrumenthood and objecthood through limitation and non-limitation; he gives an example; with the sun limited by the eye, as the eye; like the sun situated in the sky; thus seeing the pure Self, the seer of the Self

entries.transliteration: nivṛttāni buddhy-avasthānāni jāgrad-ādīni yasya saḥ | ata eva dūrī-bhūtam anya-darśanaṃ yasya | ātmanāhaṅkārāvacchinnenātmānaṃ śuddham upalabhya | ekasyaivāvacchedānavacchedābhyāṃ karaṇa-karmatve dṛṣṭāntam āha---cakṣuṣā cakṣur-avacchinnenārkeṇa gagana-stham arkam iva | evam ātma-dṛk śuddham ātmānaṃ paśyan ||10||

entries.sanskrit: मुक्त-लिङ्गं निरुपाधिकम् असति मिथ्या-भूतेऽहङ्कारे सद्-आभासं सद्-रूपेणाभासमानं ब्रह्म प्राप्नोति । शुद्ध-जीव-स्वरूपाद् विशेषम् आह---सतः कारणस्य प्रधानस्य बन्धुम् अधिष्ठानम् । असतः कार्यस्य चक्षुर् इव प्रकाशकम् । सर्वेषु कार्य-कारणेष्व् अनुस्यूतम् । अद्वयं परिपूर्णम् ॥११॥
word_for_word: free from the liṅga [body], without limiting adjunct
when ego is absent and unreal
he attains Brahman, appearing as the reflection of Reality and appearing in the form of Reality
he states the distinction from the pure nature of the jīva
the support and basis of the existent cause, Pradhāna
the illuminator of the non-existent effect, like an eye
entries.literal_english: free from the liṅga [body], without limiting adjunct; when ego is absent and unreal; he attains Brahman, appearing as the reflection of Reality and appearing in the form of Reality; he states the distinction from the pure nature of the jīva; the support and basis of the existent cause, Pradhāna; the illuminator of the non-existent effect, like an eye; pervading all effects and causes; nondual, complete

entries.transliteration: mukta-liṅgaṃ nirupādhikam asati mithyā-bhūte’haṅkāre sad-ābhāsaṃ sad-rūpeṇābhāsamānaṃ brahma prāpnoti | śuddha-jīva-svarūpād viśeṣam āha---sataḥ kāraṇasya pradhānasya bandhum adhiṣṭhānam | asataḥ kāryasya cakṣur iva prakāśakam | sarveṣu kārya-kāraṇeṣv anusyūtam | advayaṃ paripūrṇam ||11||

entries.sanskrit:
अहङ्कारोपहितेन शुद्ध-ब्रह्म-प्रतिपत्तिं सदृष्टान्तम् आह---यथेति । जले स्थित आभासः सूर्य-प्रतिबिम्बो यदा गृहान्तर्वर्ति-भित्तौ स्फुरति तदा गृह-कोण-स्थितैः पुरुषैर् भित्त्य्-आदौ स्थले स्थितेन स्वाभासेन सूर्य-प्रतिबिम्बेन यथा प्रथमं जल-स्थ आभासोऽवदृश्यते लक्ष्यते, गगन-स्थस्य गृह-मध्ये प्रतिबिम्बायोगात् । चार्थे तथा-शब्दः । यथा चेत्य् अर्थः । यथा च जल-स्थेन दिवि स्थितः सूर्यो लक्ष्यते ॥१२॥

एवं भूतेन्द्रिय-मनो-मयैः देहेन्द्रिय-मनोभिर् अवच्छिन्नैः स्वाभासैर् आत्म-प्रतिबिम्बैस् त्रि-वृत् त्रि-गुणोऽहङ्कारः सतो ब्रह्मण आभासो यस्मिंस् तेन रूपेण लक्षितः । अहङ्कार-स्थाभासं विना विषयाभासानुत्पत्तेः । अनेन चाहङ्कारेण सद्-आभास-वता सत्य-दृक् परमार्थ-ज्ञप्ति-रूप आत्मा लक्षित इत्य् अर्थः ॥१३॥
word_for_word: he explains with an example, beginning with “as”
the reflection of the sun situated in water
when it shines on an interior wall of a house
then by persons standing in a corner of the house
by the sun’s reflection, with its own appearance, situated on the wall and other place
just as first the reflection situated in water is seen and recognized
because the one situated in the sky cannot be reflected in the middle of the house
the word “tathā” is used in the sense of “and”
यथा च जल-स्थेन दिवि स्थितः सूर्यो लक्ष्यते
and as the sun situated in the sky is perceived through the one situated in water
thus, by those made of the elements, senses, and mind
limited by body, senses, and mind
by their own appearances, the reflections of the Self
in which there is the appearance of existent Brahman
because without the appearance situated in ego, the appearance of objects does not arise
by this ego possessing the appearance of Reality
the Self, whose vision is truth and whose form is ultimate awareness, is indicated
entries.literal_english: by the [Self] conditioned by ego; the realization of pure Brahman; he explains with an example, beginning with “as”; the reflection of the sun situated in water; when it shines on an interior wall of a house; then by persons standing in a corner of the house; by the sun’s reflection, with its own appearance, situated on the wall and other place; just as first the reflection situated in water is seen and recognized; because the one situated in the sky cannot be reflected in the middle of the house; the word “tathā” is used in the sense of “and”; “yathā” means “as”; and as the sun situated in the sky is perceived through the one situated in water; thus, by those made of the elements, senses, and mind; limited by body, senses, and mind; by their own appearances, the reflections of the Self; the threefold, three-guṇa ego; in which there is the appearance of existent Brahman; is indicated by that form; because without the appearance situated in ego, the appearance of objects does not arise; by this ego possessing the appearance of Reality; the Self, whose vision is truth and whose form is ultimate awareness, is indicated; this is the meaning

entries.transliteration:
ahaṅkāropahitena śuddha-brahma-pratipattiṃ sadṛṣṭāntam āha---yatheti | jale sthita ābhāsaḥ sūrya-pratibimbo yadā gṛhāntarvarti-bhittau sphurati tadā gṛha-koṇa-sthitaiḥ puruṣair bhitty-ādau sthale sthitena svābhāsena sūrya-pratibimbena yathā prathamaṃ jala-stha ābhāso’vadṛśyate lakṣyate, gagana-sthasya gṛha-madhye pratibimbāyogāt | cārthe tathā-śabdaḥ | yathā cety arthaḥ | yathā ca jala-sthena divi sthitaḥ sūryo lakṣyate ||12||

evaṃ bhūtendriya-mano-mayaiḥ dehendriya-manobhir avacchinnaiḥ svābhāsair ātma-pratibimbais tri-vṛt tri-guṇo’haṅkāraḥ sato brahmaṇa ābhāso yasmiṃs tena rūpeṇa lakṣitaḥ | ahaṅkāra-sthābhāsaṃ vinā viṣayābhāsānutpatteḥ | anena cāhaṅkāreṇa sad-ābhāsa-vatā satya-dṛk paramārtha-jñapti-rūpa ātmā lakṣita ity arthaḥ ||13||

entries.sanskrit:
इदानीं सुषुप्ति-साक्षित्वेन शुद्धात्म-प्रतिपत्तिम् अनुभवतो दर्शयति त्रिभिः । भूतादिष्व् असत्य् असत्-तुल्येऽव्याकृते निद्रया लीनेषु सत्सु यस् तत्र तदा विनिद्रो निरहङ्क्रियस् तम् आत्मानं प्रतिपद्यत इति तृतीयेनान्वयः ॥१४॥

ननु यदि तदा विनिद्रोऽसाव् अस्ति तर्हि जाग्रत्-स्वप्नयोर् इव स्फुटः किं नावभासते तत्राह---पूर्वं स द्रष्टातो द्रष्टृत्वेन स-विकल्पतया स्फुटं प्रतीतः । सुषुप्तौ तु भूतादेर् अहङ्कार-विषयस्य लीनत्वात् तद् विषयेऽहङ्कारे नष्टे सति स्वयम् अनष्टोऽपि मृषैवात्मानं नष्टवन् मन्यमानो यः । अन्यस्य नाशेऽन्यस्य नष्ट-तुल्यत्वे दृष्टान्तः, नष्ट-वित्तो यथा आतुरो विवशः, नष्टवद् भवतीत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥

ननु सुषुप्तौ न किञ्चिद् अनुभूयते, मैवम्, "सुखम् अहम् अस्वाप्सं न किञ्चिद् अवेदिषम्" इति विशेष-ज्ञानं विना केवलस्यात्मनः प्रतिसन्धानाद् इत्य् आह---एवम् इति । ननु प्रतिसन्धाने साहङ्कारस्य प्रतीतेः कथं निरहङ्क्रियत्वं तत्राह---साहङ्कारस्य द्रव्यस्य कार्य-कारण-सङ्घातस्यानुग्रहः प्रकाशकः अवस्थानं च । द्रव्य-विशेषणतयाहङ्कारस्यापि दृश्यत्वाच् च तद् द्रष्टात्मा तद् व्यतिरिक्तः । तम् आत्मानम् इत्य् अन्वयः ॥१६॥
word_for_word: इदानीं सुषुप्ति-साक्षित्वेन शुद्धात्म-प्रतिपत्तिम् अनुभवतो दर्शयति त्रिभिः
now, by three [verses], he shows the realization of the pure Self by one experiencing it as the witness of deep sleep
when the elements and the rest, unreal, like the unreal, unmanifest
who then there is sleepless and without ego
this is the connection with the third [verse/word]
तर्हि जाग्रत्-स्वप्नयोर् इव स्फुटः किं नावभासते
why is he not clearly manifest as in waking and dream?
पूर्वं स द्रष्टातो द्रष्टृत्वेन स-विकल्पतया स्फुटं प्रतीतः
before, he the seer is clearly perceived as the seer, with distinctions
but in deep sleep, because the objects beginning with the elements are dissolved
when the ego concerning those objects has been destroyed
स्वयम् अनष्टोऽपि मृषैवात्मानं नष्टवन् मन्यमानो यः
although himself not destroyed, thinking himself, through illusion, as if destroyed
the example of one seeming destroyed when another is destroyed
like a distressed, helpless person who has lost his wealth
he becomes as if destroyed—this is the meaning
one experiences nothing in deep sleep
सुखम् अहम् अस्वाप्सं न किञ्चिद् अवेदिषम्
because of recollection of the pure Self without specific knowledge
ननु प्रतिसन्धाने साहङ्कारस्य प्रतीतेः कथं निरहङ्क्रियत्वम्
if the ego-connected [entity] is perceived in recollection, how is there absence of ego?
साहङ्कारस्य द्रव्यस्य कार्य-कारण-सङ्घातस्य अनुग्रहः प्रकाशकः अवस्थानं च
the support, illumination, and existence of the aggregate of effects and causes endowed with ego
because ego too is visible as a qualifier of the substance
the Self, the seer of it, is different from it
entries.literal_english: now, by three [verses], he shows the realization of the pure Self by one experiencing it as the witness of deep sleep; when the elements and the rest, unreal, like the unreal, unmanifest; having been dissolved by sleep; who then there is sleepless and without ego; he realizes that Self; this is the connection with the third [verse/word]; if he is sleepless then; why is he not clearly manifest as in waking and dream?; before, he the seer is clearly perceived as the seer, with distinctions; but in deep sleep, because the objects beginning with the elements are dissolved; when the ego concerning those objects has been destroyed; although himself not destroyed, thinking himself, through illusion, as if destroyed; the example of one seeming destroyed when another is destroyed; like a distressed, helpless person who has lost his wealth; he becomes as if destroyed—this is the meaning; one experiences nothing in deep sleep; not so; “I slept happily; I knew nothing”; because of recollection of the pure Self without specific knowledge; therefore he says “thus”; if the ego-connected [entity] is perceived in recollection, how is there absence of ego?; the support, illumination, and existence of the aggregate of effects and causes endowed with ego; because ego too is visible as a qualifier of the substance; the Self, the seer of it, is different from it; the connection is “that Self”

entries.transliteration:
idānīṃ suṣupti-sākṣitvena śuddhātma-pratipattim anubhavato darśayati tribhiḥ | bhūtādiṣv asaty asat-tulye’vyākṛte nidrayā līneṣu satsu yas tatra tadā vinidro nirahaṅkriyas tam ātmānaṃ pratipadyata iti tṛtīyenānvayaḥ ||14||

nanu yadi tadā vinidro’sāv asti tarhi jāgrat-svapnayor iva sphuṭaḥ kiṃ nāvabhāsate tatrāha---pūrvaṃ sa draṣṭāto draṣṭṛtvena sa-vikalpatayā sphuṭaṃ pratītaḥ | suṣuptau tu bhūtāder ahaṅkāra-viṣayasya līnatvāt tad viṣaye’haṅkāre naṣṭe sati svayam anaṣṭo’pi mṛṣaivātmānaṃ naṣṭavan manyamāno yaḥ | anyasya nāśe’nyasya naṣṭa-tulyatve dṛṣṭāntaḥ, naṣṭa-vitto yathā āturo vivaśaḥ, naṣṭavad bhavatīty arthaḥ ||15||

nanu suṣuptau na kiñcid anubhūyate, maivam, "sukham aham asvāpsaṃ na kiñcid avediṣam" iti viśeṣa-jñānaṃ vinā kevalasyātmanaḥ pratisandhānād ity āha---evam iti | nanu pratisandhāne sāhaṅkārasya pratīteḥ kathaṃ nirahaṅkriyatvaṃ tatrāha---sāhaṅkārasya dravyasya kārya-kāraṇa-saṅghātasyānugrahaḥ prakāśakaḥ avasthānaṃ ca | dravya-viśeṣaṇatayāhaṅkārasyāpi dṛśyatvāc ca tad draṣṭātmā tad vyatiriktaḥ | tam ātmānam ity anvayaḥ ||16||

entries.sanskrit: भक्ति-विरक्तिभ्यां सत्य् अपि विवेके प्रकृति-पुरुषयोः परस्पर-त्यागाभावात् कतहं मुक्तिर् इति पृच्छति, पुरुषम् इति चतुर्भिः । पुरुष-व्यतिरेकेण प्रकृतेः स्वरूप-लाभाभावात् प्रकृति-व्यतिरेकेण पुरुषस्याभिव्यक्त्य्-अभावाद् इत्य् अन्योन्यापाश्रयत्वान् नित्यत्वाच् च पुरुषं प्रकृतिः कदाचिन् न मुञ्चतीत्य् अर्थः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: although discrimination is present through devotion and detachment
because Prakṛti and Puruṣa do not abandon one another
because Prakṛti does not attain her own nature apart from Puruṣa
because Puruṣa has no manifestation apart from Prakṛti
thus, because of mutual dependence and eternality
पुरुषं प्रकृतिः कदाचिन् न मुञ्चतीत्य् अर्थः
the meaning is that Prakṛti never releases Puruṣa
entries.literal_english: although discrimination is present through devotion and detachment; because Prakṛti and Puruṣa do not abandon one another; he asks, “how is there liberation?”; with four [verses] beginning with “puruṣam”; because Prakṛti does not attain her own nature apart from Puruṣa; because Puruṣa has no manifestation apart from Prakṛti; thus, because of mutual dependence and eternality; the meaning is that Prakṛti never releases Puruṣa

entries.transliteration: bhakti-viraktibhyāṃ saty api viveke prakṛti-puruṣayoḥ paraspara-tyāgābhāvāt katahaṃ muktir iti pṛcchati, puruṣam iti caturbhiḥ | puruṣa-vyatirekeṇa prakṛteḥ svarūpa-lābhābhāvāt prakṛti-vyatirekeṇa puruṣasyābhivyakty-abhāvād ity anyonyāpāśrayatvān nityatvāc ca puruṣaṃ prakṛtiḥ kadācin na muñcatīty arthaḥ ||17||

entries.sanskrit: ततः किम् अत आह---अकर्तुर् इति । ये गुणा आश्रयो यस्य सः । तेषु प्रकृतेर् गुणेषु सत्सु पुरुषस्य कैवल्यं कथम् ? ॥१९॥
word_for_word: then what follows? he says, beginning with “of the non-agent”
one for whom the guṇas are the support
while the guṇas of Prakṛti exist
entries.literal_english: then what follows? he says, beginning with “of the non-agent”; one for whom the guṇas are the support; while the guṇas of Prakṛti exist; how can Puruṣa’s isolation/liberation be [possible]?
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
entries.transliteration: tataḥ kim ata āha---akartur iti | ye guṇā āśrayo yasya saḥ | teṣu prakṛter guṇeṣu satsu puruṣasya kaivalyaṃ katham ? ||19||

entries.sanskrit: अत एव क्वचिन् निवृत्त-प्रायस्यापि संसार-भयस्य पुनर् उद्भवो दृश्यत इत्य् आह---क्वचिद् इति ॥२०॥
word_for_word: क्वचिन् निवृत्त-प्रायस्यापि संसार-भयस्य पुनर् उद्भवो दृश्यते
the re-arising of fear of saṃsāra, though almost ceased somewhere, is seen
entries.literal_english: therefore, for this very reason; the re-arising of fear of saṃsāra, though almost ceased somewhere, is seen; he says, beginning with “somewhere”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact chapter marker preserved.
entries.transliteration: ata eva kvacin nivṛtta-prāyasyāpi saṃsāra-bhayasya punar udbhavo dṛśyata ity āha---kvacid iti ||20||

entries.sanskrit: न हि प्रकृति-संबन्ध-मात्रं बन्ध-हेतुः, किन्तु गुण-बुद्ध्या तद्-आसक्तिस् तन्-निवृत्तौ सत्यां मोक्षो घटते । क्वचिद् उद्भवस् तु साधन-वैकल्याद् इत्य् अभिप्रेत्य साधनातिशयं कथयन् परिहरति त्रिभिः । निमित्तं फलम् । तन् न निमित्तं प्रवर्तकं यस्मिन्, तेन निष्कामेन धर्मेण । अमलात्मना निर्मलेन मनसा । श्रुतेन कथा-श्रवणेन संभृतया पुष्टया ॥२१॥ दह्यमाना अभिभूयमाना तिरो-हिता भवति ॥२३॥
word_for_word: mere connection with Prakṛti is not the cause of bondage
rather, attachment to it through thinking it to be the guṇas
its re-arising somewhere is due to deficiency of the means
इत्य् अभिप्रेत्य साधनातिशयं कथयन् परिहरति त्रिभिः
intending this, he states the excellence of the means and refutes [the objection] in three [verses]
that in which it is not the motive or impelling cause
being burned and overcome, it becomes hidden
entries.literal_english: mere connection with Prakṛti is not the cause of bondage; rather, attachment to it through thinking it to be the guṇas; when that ceases, liberation occurs; its re-arising somewhere is due to deficiency of the means; intending this, he states the excellence of the means and refutes [the objection] in three [verses]; the result is the motive; that in which it is not the motive or impelling cause; through that desireless dharma; with a stainless, pure mind; nourished by hearing the narration; being burned and overcome, it becomes hidden

entries.transliteration: na hi prakṛti-saṃbandha-mātraṃ bandha-hetuḥ, kintu guṇa-buddhyā tad-āsaktis tan-nivṛttau satyāṃ mokṣo ghaṭate | kvacid udbhavas tu sādhana-vaikalyād ity abhipretya sādhanātiśayaṃ kathayan pariharati tribhiḥ | nimittaṃ phalam | tan na nimittaṃ pravartakaṃ yasmin, tena niṣkāmena dharmeṇa | amalātmanā nirmalena manasā | śrutena kathā-śravaṇena saṃbhṛtayā puṣṭayā ||21|| dahyamānā abhibhūyamānā tiro-hitā bhavati ||23||

entries.sanskrit: प्रतिबुद्धार्थो विदितात्म-तत्त्वः । कैवल्याख्यं स्व-संस्थानं देहादि-व्यतिरिक्तं स्वरूपं मद्-आश्रयं निःश्रेयसं निरतिशयानन्दम् ॥२८॥
word_for_word: who knows the truth of the Self
the nature distinct from the body and the rest
entries.literal_english: one whose understanding has awakened; who knows the truth of the Self; one’s own state called kaivalya; the nature distinct from the body and the rest; having Me as its shelter; the highest good, unsurpassed bliss

entries.transliteration: pratibuddhārtho viditātma-tattvaḥ | kaivalyākhyaṃ sva-saṃsthānaṃ dehādi-vyatiriktaṃ svarūpaṃ mad-āśrayaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ niratiśayānandam ||28||

entries.sanskrit: तदा त्व् अणिमादि-सिद्धयोऽन्तराय-रूपा भवन्ति । तासु योगेनोपचितासु समृद्धासु न योगाद् अन्यो हेतुर् यासां, तासु यदा सिद्धस्य चेतो न विषज्जते । अङ्ग ! हे मातः ! अथ तदा अन्तम् अतिक्रान्तोऽत्यन्तो योऽहं, तत्-सम्बन्धिनी । यत्र यस्यां गतौ मृत्योर् हासो न भवति । विषक्टौ तु सिद्धोऽपि मया वशी-कृत इति मृत्योर् हासो गर्वो भवतीत्य् अर्थः ॥३०॥
word_for_word: then the perfections beginning with aṇimā become obstacles
when they have been cultivated by yoga and become perfected
न योगाद् अन्यो हेतुर् यासां तासु
those for which there is no other cause than yoga
when the mind of the perfected one does not cling
then [there is] I, who am beyond the limit, the highest
that which is related to Me
यत्र यस्यां गतौ मृत्योर् हासो न भवति
in which state of attainment there is no diminution of death
विषक्टौ तु सिद्धोऽपि मया वशी-कृत इति
but when attached [to objects], even the perfected one is controlled by Me
death’s laughter becomes pride—this is the meaning
entries.literal_english: then the perfections beginning with aṇimā become obstacles; when they have been cultivated by yoga and become perfected; those for which there is no other cause than yoga; when the mind of the perfected one does not cling; O dear one, O mother!; then [there is] I, who am beyond the limit, the highest; that which is related to Me; in which state of attainment there is no diminution of death; but when attached [to objects], even the perfected one is controlled by Me; death’s laughter becomes pride—this is the meaning

entries.transliteration: tadā tv aṇimādi-siddhayo’ntarāya-rūpā bhavanti | tāsu yogenopacitāsu samṛddhāsu na yogād anyo hetur yāsāṃ, tāsu yadā siddhasya ceto na viṣajjate | aṅga ! he mātaḥ ! atha tadā antam atikrānto’tyanto yo’haṃ, tat-sambandhinī | yatra yasyāṃ gatau mṛtyor hāso na bhavati | viṣakṭau tu siddho’pi mayā vaśī-kṛta iti mṛtyor hāso garvo bhavatīty arthaḥ ||30||
